title: Wave Properties
learning_goal: Investigate and calculate relationships among wave speed, frequency, wavelength, and amplitude.

stages.title: 1. Describe a wave
stages.content: Amplitude describes maximum displacement from equilibrium. Wavelength λ is the distance between corresponding points on successive waves. Frequency f is the number of cycles per second.

stages.title: 2. Wave speed relationship
stages.content: Wave speed is related to frequency and wavelength by v = fλ.

stages.title: 3. Units
stages.content: Wave speed is measured in m/s, frequency in hertz (Hz), and wavelength in meters.

stages.title: 4. Worked example
stages.content: A wave has frequency 5 Hz and wavelength 2 m. Its speed is v = fλ = 5 × 2 = 10 m/s.

stages.title: 5. Guided practice
stages.prompt: A wave travels at 24 m/s with a frequency of 6 Hz. What is its wavelength?
stages.hint: Rearrange v = fλ to λ = v/f.
stages.alternate_explanation: Wavelength is how far the wave travels during one cycle, so divide speed by cycles per second.

stages.title: 6. Mastery check
stages.content: To demonstrate mastery, define amplitude, frequency, wavelength, and wave speed, use v = fλ, rearrange the equation correctly, and interpret how changing frequency or wavelength affects wave speed in a given medium.

concept_cards.content: Wave speed is related to frequency and wavelength by v = fλ.

concept_cards.title: A wave has frequency 5 Hz and wavelength 2 m. What is its speed?
concept_cards.content: v = fλ = 5 × 2 = 10 m/s. Frequency counts cycles per second and wavelength measures distance per cycle.

concept_cards.content: λ = v/f. At fixed wave speed, frequency and wavelength vary inversely.
